transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess it’s my eating, doctor. It’s a little embarrassing to say. Sometimes when I start on certain comfort foods, I tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough now,” but then my hand just goes back to the pot anyway. It feels like I can’t quite make myself stop, if that makes sense.
Can you describe how long these episodes usually last when you find yourself continuing to eat even though you told yourself to stop?

I’m not sure I’ve really timed it, doctor. It doesn’t feel like an all-day thing, usually… more like I look up and realize I’ve been at it longer than I meant to. I’m sorry, I know that’s not very exact. I just haven’t kept track.
During these times when you find yourself continuing to eat even though you told yourself to stop, do you notice yourself eating much more quickly than usual?

Yes… I think I do, doctor. I’ve always been a slow eater, really, but lately when this happens, I’ll be standing there by the counter and eating faster than I normally would. It’s like I hardly taste it before the next bite is already in my mouth. I’m not proud of that, but… yes, I have noticed it.
During these episodes, do you feel like you’ve lost control over how much you’re eating, even if you want to stop?

Yes… I think that’s the part that worries me, doctor. Once I start on those comfort foods, I’ll tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough now,” and I really do mean it… but then my hand goes right back to the pot. It feels like I’m not quite able to make myself stop, even though I want to.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of eating much more quickly than usual, feeling a loss of control over eating, and being unable to stop even when intending to, supports a diagnosis of Binge Eating Disorder (F50.01). Other candidates such as F50.00 (Anorexia Nervosa) or F50.02 (Bulimia Nervosa) can be ruled out due to absence of key features like restrictive eating, fear of weight gain, or compensatory behaviors like purging. The presentation does not align with atypical presentations (F50.80, F50.81, F50.88), which require less specific or different criteria.
